title: Agentic AI Testing Platform configuration
description: Wiring for an installed platform: where the Tool Root's data lives, which repository is the Target Project, and what the platform may read and write inside it. See pipeline.md §13 and platform_core/tools/platform_paths/README.md.

$schema.description: Editor hint. Ignored by the resolver.

configVersion.description: Schema version. A value this build does not support is a hard error, never a best-effort read.

mode.description: 'installed' — the tool folder sits inside a separate Target Project. 'self-hosted' — the platform tests its own repository (targetRoot === toolRoot); used by this repo's examples/ fixture.

targetRoot.description: The Target Project's root, relative to THIS FILE's directory (absolute permitted for a detached install). Required when mode is 'installed'; never inferred at runtime. Typically "..".

dataRoot.description: Where every process artifact lives, relative to the Tool Root. Must resolve inside the Tool Root.

target.description: What the platform may do inside the Target Project (pipeline.md §13.2-§13.4). All paths are relative to targetRoot.

testDirs.description: Detected or declared test directories by kind. Written by `agentic-testing init` from detectTestDirs().

automationRoot.description: The single directory generated automation is written to. Required whenever writeAllowlist is non-empty.

writeAllowlist.description: Glob patterns the platform may write. FAIL-CLOSED: empty or absent means the platform writes nothing to the Target Project and Stage 5 generates inside platform_core_data/ instead. Supports **, * and ?.

readDenylist.description: Additional never-read patterns. MERGED WITH, never replacing, the non-overridable built-in list (.env*, **/credentials*.json, **/secrets*, **/*.pem, **/*.key, **/.aws/**, **/id_rsa*).

detectedStack.description: Cached result of the last detection. Advisory only — a stage re-detects rather than trusting this.

git.description: Which repository the automation lifecycle's git operations act on (pipeline.md §12.4).

mode.description: 'tool-repo' (default) — the tool folder is its own nested git repository, so baseline three-way-merge protection always works and no commit ever lands in the host's history. 'host-repo' — commit artifacts into the Target Project's repository (restricted to paths under dataRoot). 'off' — no git; the lifecycle runs in degraded, filesystem-only mode and says so.

commitBaseline.description: When false, an approved merge writes baseline files but stages and commits nothing, leaving the commit to a human.
